This vignette covers the contracts a method must satisfy:

* its **first argument** is the data realization;
* its **remaining arguments** must be drawn from
  `parameter_grid ∪ fixed_parameters` (and `B` if `batched = TRUE`);
* it should be **deterministic given a seed** — `simulatr` controls
  RNG state per replicate; the method should not call `set.seed()`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(simulatr)
```

# A non-batched method (the common case)

The data realization is whatever the model's `generate` function
returned. Method-side parameters resolve from the grid by name.

```{r}
ridge <- simulatr_method(
  name = "ridge",
  run = function(data, lambda) {
    XtX <- crossprod(data$X)
    p   <- ncol(XtX)
    beta_hat <- solve(XtX + lambda * diag(p), crossprod(data$X, data$y))
    list(beta = as.numeric(beta_hat))
  }
)
```

`lambda` here must be a column of `parameter_grid` or an entry of
`fixed_parameters`; otherwise the call to `simulatr_study()` errors
with the offending name.

# A batched method (`batched = TRUE`)

For methods with non-trivial setup — fitting one model per `(n, p)`
pair across many bootstrap replicates, for example — `batched = TRUE`
lets `simulatr` hand the method a length-`B` *list* of data
realizations at once. The `run` function must return a `B`-row tibble
with columns `run_id` (int) and `output` (list).

```{r}
boot_se <- simulatr_method(
  name = "boot_se",
  run = function(draws, B) {
    out <- vector("list", B)
    for (b in seq_len(B)) {
      fit <- lm.fit(draws[[b]]$X, draws[[b]]$y)
      out[[b]] <- list(beta = unname(fit$coefficients))
    }
    tibble::tibble(run_id = seq_len(B), output = out)
  },
  batched = TRUE
)
```

Use `batched = TRUE` when the per-replicate setup cost dominates the
per-replicate work; otherwise, leave it `FALSE` (the default) and let
`simulatr_run()` interleave generation and method application
one replicate at a time so peak memory scales with one draw, not `B`.

# Randomized methods and the RNG protocol

`simulatr` uses one seed per replicate:

```
seed_b = study@fixed_parameters$seed + run_id
```

Generation and method application within a replicate share that seed.
A randomized method (lasso with random folds, a bootstrap, MCMC
initialization) is fed a fresh state for every `run_id`, so two
replicates with the same `run_id` reproduce bit-for-bit and two
replicates with different `run_id` give independent draws. The method
itself should not call `set.seed()` — that breaks the protocol and the
results stop being reproducible.

The same protocol means **reordering rows of `parameter_grid` does not
perturb seeds**. Adding or deleting a grid row only affects that row's
draws.

# Declaring required packages

If your method needs a package that isn't a base/`Imports` dependency,
declare it on the method:

```{r}
glmnet_method <- simulatr_method(
  name = "glmnet",
  run = function(data) {
    fit <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(data$X, data$y, intercept = FALSE)
    list(beta = as.numeric(glmnet::coef.glmnet(fit, s = "lambda.1se"))[-1L])
  },
  packages = "glmnet"
)
```

The pipeline uses `packages` to install dependencies into worker
containers; on the laptop, `simulatr_run()` only verifies they are
loadable.

# Errors are captured, not fatal

A method that throws an error on a single replicate does not abort the
study. The error is captured per-replicate and surfaced in the
`results` tibble's `output` list-column as a `simulatr_error` object;
metrics on those replicates return `NA` and the summary's `n` decreases
accordingly. A benign warning is also captured (via
`withCallingHandlers`) — it does not erase the row's results.

# Settings vs. parameters

Use a method's `settings` slot for things that are not part of the
sweep — a default lambda grid, a precomputed kernel matrix. Use
`parameter_grid` columns for anything you sweep over. The construction
contract checks formals against the grid; settings are private to the
method.
